text:
tobi: Quick sync: rethinking private connectivity options for customers who decline VPCE/peering but need predictable control-plane auth. Goal: zero-touch onboarding + minimal network changes for customers, but maintain least-privilege and good observability. I sketched three approaches, want quick gut-checks.

viv: tl;dr please — what are the options?

tobi: Option 1) Connectorless ephemeral tunnels to regional relays (on-demand TLS tunnels). Fast for customers, no infra changes. Downside: our egress IPs are dynamic unless customer allows our CIDR.

rahul: we've debated this before. Biggest ops hit is connection churn at relays and NAT scaling. Also DDoS surface increases if many tunnels.

ops-bot: note: relays already enforce per-tenant rate limits and connection caps; scaling plan required if option rolled wide.

sasha: Option 2) Customer runs tiny connector binary that opens a single long-lived outbound connection and pins to a customer-provisioned ENI/ENI-like resource so egress IPs are stable. It's an opt-in for allowlist customers.

viv: this seems pragmatic: most security-conscious customers will accept a tiny binary or AMI. But that adds onboarding complexity and lifecycle (updates, rotation).

evan: Option 3) Hybrid: default to connectorless ephemeral tunnels, offer a "static-egress" add-on where we provide a managed small gateway in the customer account (cloudformation/terraform) that maps traffic to a stable IP. That is between full peering and pure operatorless.

rahul: hybrid reduces blast radius vs giving full peering. But we'll need a minimal operator role or infra-ops playbook to support the managed gateway.

viv: security question: how does control-plane auth work in each option?

tobi: Proposal: issue short-lived certs minted from control plane after a scoped onboarding flow. Flow: customer creates scoped onboarding token -> call to /auth/exchange -> returns short cert with 5 min lifetime used for TLS mTLS to relays/gateway. We avoid long-lived static credentials.

sasha: short certs good. Ops preference is to keep TTL very short and rely on revocation by rotation instead of CRLs. Also log token creation with principal.

ops-bot: reminder: must surface audit logs to customers on onboarding events. Ticket created: SEC-2401 (link: https://go/sec/SEC-2401).

evan: for the managed-gateway variant we need IAM roles + CloudFormation templates. Keep everything read-only except the minimal network pieces.

rahul: performance: tunnel adds ~8-20ms median at regional edge depending on provider. That may be acceptable for most ingestion/async workloads, but not for sub-30ms interactive inference. We should document recommended patterns: Peering/VPCE for <50ms SLOs; static-managed gateway for allowlist; ephemeral by default.

viv: rollout plan?

tobi: Suggested rollout: preview with non-prod customers (10 accounts) using connectorless. Collect these metrics: handshake_ms p50/p95, conn_keepalive_secs, relays_per_region, NAT_bandwidth_by_tenant, error_rate. Add SDK flag to surface "connectivity_mode" in telemetry.

sasha: also add a metric for "controlplane_auth_fail" and a breakdown by token error vs cert error. Useful for debugging onboarding flows.

rahul: ops concerns: path MTU fragmentation with tunnels. Add an e2e check as part of CI: spinup VPC in AWS/GCP, run UDP/TCP PMTU probe, ensure 1500 -> 1430 margins ok.

evan: implement ALPN multiplexing on 443 so customers behind strict egress rules only need port 443. No custom ports.

viv: what about customer allowlist teams who refuse any outbound traffic to unknown IPs?

tobi: for those, managed-gateway or connector with pinned ENI is the only option. Provide IaC plus a short-run operator onboarding to install and optionally rotate certs via SSM.

sasha: one more security item: narrow scope tokens. When customer requests a token, require an explicit checkbox: "allow agentless connectivity" and list regions. Tokens scoped to regions reduce blast radius.

ops-bot: action items created: ARCH-conn-preview-metrics, INFRA-pmtu-test, SEC-shortcert-audit (links: https://go/arch/ARCH-conn-preview-metrics).

rahul: cost model: need to estimate NAT egress cost and relay connection cost. Quick back-of-envelope: if 500k daily connectors with 60s keepalive => 500k * (1/60) new connections/sec ~8.3k conn/s sustained. Add NAT throughput headroom. This informs relay autoscale.

viv: good to capture in RFC. Also add rollout gating: p95 handshake < 300ms and no CPU pressure on relays over 70% for preview customers.

evan: SDK and docs: add clear error codes: CONNECTOR_MODE=ephemeral|gateway|pinned; errors: 1001(handshake_timeout),1002(cert_expired),1003(egress_blocked).

tobi: Decision leaning: adopt default connectorless ephemeral tunnels + hybrid managed gateway for allowlist customers + option for customer-managed pinned connector. Next steps: I'll draft RFC with the following sections: Goals, Options with diagrams, Security flow, Telemetry and SLOs, Testing matrix, Cost estimate. Will post for review next week.

viv: +1 from me. Please include runbooks for revocation and incident playbook for mass connection failures.

sasha: +1. Also request a small prototype that demonstrates the auth exchange flow and a smoke relay we can use for perf tests.

tobi: thanks. I'll create the RFC draft and link here. If anyone wants to join a short design sess, ping me. :calendar:
